If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimation.

If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract downward bias.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and true price rises >1.5% from 10-day avg, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for late horizon (16–30 days) to capture momentum.

If sentiment spikes from negative to positive within 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 1.0–2.0% in the first 5 days to correct for sentiment reversal lag.

If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.5% per day for late horizon to prevent overcorrection.

If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, increase forecast slope by 0.2–0.5% per day for early horizon to offset bearish drift.
